policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'worshippeth' renders the action but does not distinguish the qere יִסְגָּד from the ketiv יסגוד; no mapped textual note decides between them, so both readings remain compatible and the base fallback is retained.
ASV explicitly reads '(who is with me?)', which renders the ketiv מי אתי; the mapped textual_variant note gives 'by myself' only as another reading, confirming that the main ASV wording selects r01.
